questions.explanation: Move the x-terms to one side: subtracting 4x and adding 9 gives 12 > 3x, and dividing by the positive 3 gives x < 4. The value 3 works because 4(3) + 3 = 15 beats 7(3) - 9 = 12, while x = 4 gives 19 on both sides and fails the strict test. Adding 9 to the wrong side shifts the boundary to 13, and the whole-number answer below 4 is 3.
questions.hint: Subtract the x-terms from both sides before dividing by the coefficient.

questions.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides to get -2y >= x - 6, then divide by the negative 2, which flips the direction: y <= (x - 6) / (-2) = -1/2x + 3. Test (0, 0): the original gives 6 >= 0 and the rewrite gives 0 <= 3; test (0, 4): the original fails and 4 <= 3 also fails, so the two agree. Dropping the negative or keeping the sign gives a different region.
questions.hint: Isolate y, remembering that dividing by a negative reverses the inequality sign.
questions.learningObjective: rewrite an inequality in graphing form with y isolated

questions.explanation: The greater-than sign is strict, so 5 is not part of the solution and the boundary needs an open dot; the shading to the right of 5 is already correct. A closed dot claims x = 5 works, but 5 > 5 is false. Shading left would describe x < 5 instead, and shading a single dot throws away the whole interval above 5.
